notes.scope: West African gold exploitation: selected modern mines and two separately identified historical gold-producing districts. Not an exhaustive mining cadastre.
notes.temporalMethod: Only reviewed operating intervals are displayed. Coverage gaps do not necessarily mean inactivity. All periods are finite; sourceYear 2026 is a review snapshot, not an assertion of 2026 production. Annual granularity cannot express partial-year shutdowns.
notes.geographicMethod: All points are approximate mine-complex or district markers. Technical-report coordinates and CC BY 4.0 Fineprint research locations are preferred; a disclosed TSF is used as a representative complex anchor only where identified explicitly. Historical districts are coarse interpretations of published regional descriptions, never modern mines projected backwards.
notes.excluded: Galam was not added because reviewed evidence identified a trading corridor without a sufficiently separate extraction-area chronology. Stockpile-only years and construction/production guidance are excluded.

siteAudit.west-africa:bambuk: Approximate regional marker near Kéniéba, within the Senegal–Falémé goldfield described by Levtzion. Centuries normalized to integer display intervals. This district must not be merged with present-day industrial mines. The 1500/1501 boundary separates source windows, not a claimed shutdown.
siteAudit.west-africa:bure: Coarse representative point in the Upper Niger/Siguiri region described by Levtzion, not an archaeological shaft. Period is a historical regional window; no continuity into the modern Siguiri mine is inferred.
siteAudit.west-africa:ahafo-south: Fineprint facility COM00009.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table. South-site coordinate selected from the two-point Ahafo facility; Ahafo North is not backdated.
siteAudit.west-africa:akyem: Fineprint facility COM00016.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table.
siteAudit.west-africa:bibiani: Fineprint facility COM00130.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table. Restart phases are independently documented by Asante; the intervening coverage gap is retained.
siteAudit.west-africa:chirano: Fineprint facility COM00254.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table. 2019–2023 is omitted for lack of individually reviewed operating evidence, not asserted as a closure.
siteAudit.west-africa:edikan: Fineprint facility COM00368.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table.
siteAudit.west-africa:iduapriem: Fineprint facility COM00553.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table.
siteAudit.west-africa:obuasi: Fineprint facility COM00932.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table. The 2015 dataset row is excluded because the mine was in its shutdown/care-and-maintenance transition; later redevelopment is outside this entry’s reviewed coverage.
siteAudit.west-africa:siguiri: Fineprint facility COM01191.00; original reporting sources are linked in the dataset source_ids table.
siteAudit.west-africa:loulo: Separate Fineprint coordinate retained for each mine. Start is corroborated by the 2011 Form 20-F; annual production history also appears in Barrick’s 2020 Investor Day MRM presentation. No 2026 output is inferred. 2026 update: Barrick Q2 MD&A p.20 documents positive open-pit ore and underground extraction plus Q1/Q2 gold production for the combined complex; original separate coordinates are retained without allocating production between them.
siteAudit.west-africa:gounkoto: Separate Fineprint coordinate retained for each mine. Start is corroborated by the 2011 Form 20-F; annual production history also appears in Barrick’s 2020 Investor Day MRM presentation. No 2026 output is inferred. 2026 update: Barrick Q2 MD&A p.20 documents positive open-pit ore and underground extraction plus Q1/Q2 gold production for the combined complex; original separate coordinates are retained without allocating production between them.
siteAudit.west-africa:fekola: Point represents the Fekola mine complex. Technical report section 4.1 provides the approximate coordinate; transformed EPSG:32629 to EPSG:4326. 2026 update: Q2 results dated 6 August explicitly report Fekola open-pit mining and actual gold production; regional project forecasts excluded.
siteAudit.west-africa:syama: The 2002–2007 gap is preserved. Ballo et al., The Syama and Tabakoroni goldfields, Mali, provide the mine coordinate; rounded original location is approximate. 2026 update: March quarterly report production tables show positive Syama underground and open-pit ore mining, not only oxide-stockpile processing.
siteAudit.west-africa:sadiola: Fineprint mine coordinate. Stockpile processing between April 2018 and the 2021 mining restart does not extend extraction into 2019 or 2020. 2026 update: Q2 MD&A reports 1.74 Mt ore mined and 48,080 oz produced in the quarter, with positive first-half extraction.
siteAudit.west-africa:yatela: The Fineprint Ore mined series after 2013 is not used because the primary closure announcement distinguishes excavation from continuing processing.
siteAudit.west-africa:morila: 2001 is the first reviewed annual observation, not a claim that the mine opened then. Stockpile/tailings processing after 2009 is excluded; possible other satellite phases are not inferred. Later ownership changes do not by themselves attest continued extraction.
siteAudit.west-africa:kalana: Approximate block-model centre from E586610–588520 and N1192480–1194150, EPSG:32629. Processing until December 2017 does not imply extraction after September. No future open-pit construction date is treated as production.
siteAudit.west-africa:nampala: Coordinate: 6°12′52″W, 11°09′17″N in section 6.1.1. Earlier partial start-up and shutdown episodes are omitted conservatively; 2025 forecast is not actual production. 2026 update: issuer quarterly report of 28 April 2026, Nampala table, reports 658,905 t ore mined in Q1 2026 and positive December 2025 comparative. The original 2025 technical report’s projected 2026 output is not used.
siteAudit.west-africa:yanfolila: Coarse project-centre marker. The 2015 technical report prints 8°30′E alongside an unequivocal western-Mali location; W is used, corroborated by the project map and its position west of Yanfolila. Not a precise individual pit coordinate. No production after the reviewed 2023 data is assumed.
siteAudit.west-africa:hounde: Representative point at the mine’s disclosed TSF: 11°25′3.28″N, 3°32′31.40″W. Not the exact active pit.
siteAudit.west-africa:mana: TSF representative coordinate: 11°57′20″N, 3°24′46″W. Years 2009–2014 are outside this entry’s reviewed annual operating evidence, not asserted as a shutdown.
siteAudit.west-africa:sabodala-massawa: Sabodala TSF1 representative point: 13°12′42″N, 12°11′53″W. Massawa joined the complex in 2020; its individual deposits are not backdated. The 2010–2016 evidence gap is not a closure claim.
siteAudit.west-africa:ity: Technical-report mine-centre coordinate: 6°52′16″N, 8°06′30″W. The 1992–2014 evidence gap is not a claim of closure; the 2019 CIL start is not misused as the mine’s first production.
siteAudit.west-africa:lafigue: Disclosed TSF representative point: 8°16′23.22″N, 4°39′28.39″W; not an exact individual pit.
siteAudit.west-africa:kiniero: Coordinate: 9°47′48″W, 10°25′52″N in section 7.1.1. The earlier mine is distinguished from the later redevelopment project; planned reopening is not actual extraction.
siteAudit.west-africa:agbaou: Technical-report permit-centre coordinate, 6°08′N, 5°11′W; approximate complex location rather than individual shaft.
siteAudit.west-africa:tongon: Representative TSF coordinate from Barrick’s public tailings inventory. 2025 endpoint is an attestation bound, not a mine-closure claim. Initial production is also recorded in Randgold’s 2014 Form 20-F.
siteAudit.west-africa:tarkwa: Process-plant coordinate 5°19′37″N, 2°01′17″W. Underground and open-pit phases overlap in 1999; that overlap is intentional. Earlier 1930s shaft construction is omitted because it is not itself production evidence.
siteAudit.west-africa:essakane: TSF location 0°4′18″E, 14°21′15″N is an approximate complex marker, not the active pit. No forecast reserves, mine-life estimates or 2026 guidance extend the period.

notes.mali2026Update: Quarterly production/extraction evidence reviewed for Loulo, Gounkoto, Fekola, Syama, Sadiola and Nampala. An active 2026 marker means activity documented within 2026, not a guarantee of uninterrupted production for the whole year or after the latest report. Loulo and Gounkoto share a combined complex operating report.
